The State in his counter affidavit has filed a copy of the written communication sent to the

2. Heard learned counsel for the appellant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.

The instant criminal appeal under Section 14A (2) SC/ST Act has been filed by the appellant- Rashid for grant of bail and for setting aside/quashing the impugned order dated 05.08.2024 passed by the learned Special Judge, S.C./S.T. Act, Barabanki in Bail Application No.2331 of 2024,
arising out of Case Crime/ FIR No.280 of 2024, under Section 366, 376, 506 IPC, 3/5 R.C. Act and Section 3(2)(v) S.C./S.T. Act lodged at Police Station Safdarganj, District- Barabanki, during trial.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant, while pressing the bail-appeal, submits that the appellant has Rashid vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. ...

5. It is further submitted that F.I.R. of this case has been lodged by the father of the prosecutrix on 23.06.2024 at 07.30 P.M. alleging that his daughter aged about 17 years has been enticed away by the appellant on 21.06.2024.
6.

It is vehemently submitted that the appellant has not enticed away the prosecutrix and it was the prosecutrix, who had come to the appellant and even after persuading her, she did not return to her house and had gone with him to Puna and when the appellant came to know that a false case has been lodged against him and his family members, he brought back the victim through flight and thereafter, they were apprehended by the local police.

7. To substantiate his submissions, learned counsel for the appellant has drawn the attention of this Court towards the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. as well as the statement given to the doctor, which has been recorded by the doctor at an appropriate place in the medical injury report in order to canvass that it was the prosecutrix, who was in love with the appellant and she had herself come to the house of the appellant and when he (appellant) asked her to return to her house, she refused and insisted him to marry her and thereafter, she resided with him at his accommodation and sexual relations were also established between them with the free will, wish and consent of the victim and thus, there was no element of any sexual assault and as the sexual relations were established with the consent of the prosecutrix, who as per her educational credentials was more than 18 years of age at the date and time of the alleged incident, no offence in fact has been committed by the appellant/ applicant.
8.

It is further submitted that in the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., which has been recorded after many days of her recovery, she has changed the story in terms that she was enticed away by the appellant and the sexual relations were also established without her consent and also that she was persuaded by the appellant to change her religion.
9. It is vehemently submitted that this statement has been changed by the prosecutrix on account of the pressure applied by the informant and his family members.
However, the allegations are not substantiated by any medical report.
The appellant is in jail in this case since 21.06.2024 and he is not having any criminal antecedents.
There is no apprehension that after being released on bail the applicant may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.

10. Learned A.G.A. on the other hand opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant on the ground that the prosecutrix was not only subjected to rape, but was also persuaded to change her religion and thus, the appellant is not entitled to be released on bail.
11.

Considering the fact that the prosecutrix was aged about more than 18 years at the time of the alleged incident, after her recovery no injury etc. has been found on her person and she in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and also to the doctor at the time of her medical examination has admitted to be in love with with the appellant and also to have left her home on her Rashid vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. ... on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95915141/
2 own volition and also to have entered into sexual relationship with her consent and keeping in view the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the appellant that she has changed her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. under the influence of her family members and also the period of detention of the appellant in this case, a case of bail is made out in favour of the appellant.

sentences.text: 12. In result, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order passed by the special/trial court is set-aside.
Pending application(s) shall stand disposed of.

13. Let the appellant- Rashid, involved in above- mentioned case, be released on bail, on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The appellant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The appellant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The appellant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
14.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
15. Identity, status and residence proof of the appellant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
16. Observations made herein-above by this court are only for the purpose of disposal of this bail application and shall not be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
(Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.) Order Date :- 4.10.2024
